headline: Cancer Patient Saves Stranger's Life With Quick CPR
meta_description: A 68-year-old man undergoing chemotherapy spotted a stranger in cardiac arrest and performed CPR, likely saving his life.
summary_short: A 68-year-old undergoing chemotherapy for stage 4 lung cancer witnessed a stranger collapse and sprang into action with CPR.
body:
A 68-year-old man undergoing chemotherapy for stage 4 lung cancer spotted a stranger in cardiac arrest and immediately began CPR, helping save his life. His doctor credited the rapid response with making the critical difference in the outcome.

The incident reveals an unexpected story: while facing one of life's most serious health battles, this man found himself positioned to help another person at their moment of greatest need. Rather than being consumed by his own treatment, he remained alert enough to recognize an emergency unfolding around him—and moved fast enough to act.

His doctor's assessment underscores what medical professionals know well: survival in cardiac arrest depends heavily on those first moments. The man's willingness to step in, despite his own vulnerability, turned a potential tragedy into a second chance for the stranger he helped.
